meta.description: Venture family folders and venture type objects for an entrepreneur catalogue. One folder per venture family, one object per venture type. Every object can carry one instance of a venture dossier tool.
meta.sourceNote: Curated catalogue of 499 ways to start or buy a business, from a handyman service to a state-scale project. Capital bands are realistic start-up ranges, not the cost of reaching scale. Impossible entries are deliberately included so the ceiling is visible.
meta.importNote: The importer consumes folders[] first, then objects[]. Objects are matched by slug inside their folder, so re-running the import skips a venture that already exists. The importer must ignore capitalBands, models, barriers, scales, firstRevenue definitions and objects[].reality.

importContract.folders: Create one folder per folders[] entry under the application that owns targetObjectType, keeping name, slug, code and order.
importContract.objects: Create one object per objects[] entry: name = name, slug = slug, parent folder = the folder whose slug equals family, cmsObjectType = targetObjectType.
importContract.seed: Optional: seed the html-tool field targetFieldId with { version: 1, venture: { title: name, slug: slug, family: <folder name>, oneLiner: blurb, status: 'draft' } }. The tool normalizes every missing part.
importContract.idempotency: Match objects by slug inside the folder. Skip an object that already exists; never overwrite an edited dossier.

objects.name: Small orbital launch company
objects.blurb: Develops a rocket, launch site and customers for small satellites.
objects.reality: Rocket Lab needed more than a decade and over a billion dollars to reach orbit regularly.

objects.name: Satellite internet constellation
objects.blurb: Hundreds of satellites, ground stations, spectrum and user terminals.
objects.reality: Spectrum filings, launch capacity and terminal subsidies make this a capital-markets project.

objects.name: Private space station
objects.blurb: Habitat modules, launch contracts and life-support certification.
objects.reality: Certification and rescue planning are government-grade problems.

objects.name: Space tourism operator
objects.blurb: Vehicles, training, medical screening and a licensed launch operation.
objects.reality: Insurance and licensing are as hard as the vehicle itself.

objects.name: Lunar landing and services company
objects.blurb: Landers, payload integration and contracts with space agencies.
objects.reality: Revenue depends on agency contracts awarded years in advance.

objects.name: Industrial robotics company
objects.blurb: Sells automation cells and the software that runs them.

objects.name: Humanoid robotics company
objects.blurb: Actuators, perception, control software and manufacturing partnerships.
objects.reality: Every unit is a hardware and safety problem; the field is still pre-scale.

objects.name: Drone manufacturer
objects.blurb: Builds and certifies drones for inspection, mapping and delivery.

objects.name: Quantum computing company
objects.blurb: Hardware, error correction and cloud access to a quantum machine.
objects.reality: Error correction at useful scale has not been demonstrated; expect patient science capital.

objects.name: AI foundation model lab
objects.blurb: Compute clusters, research teams and training runs at frontier scale.
objects.reality: Training runs at the frontier cost hundreds of millions per cycle.

objects.name: Semiconductor chip design company (fabless)
objects.blurb: Designs chips and outsources fabrication to a foundry.

objects.name: Gene therapy company
objects.blurb: Preclinical work, trials and manufacturing for a genetic treatment.
objects.reality: A single programme can take a decade and several hundred million dollars to reach approval.

objects.name: Neural interface company
objects.blurb: Implants, surgical robotics and clinical evidence over many years.
objects.reality: Regulators treat implants as high-risk devices; clinical evidence takes years to collect.

objects.name: Synthetic biology company
objects.blurb: Engineers organisms or enzymes and scales them into production.

objects.name: Global software platform at Microsoft scale
objects.blurb: Operating systems, productivity suites and cloud sold to most of the world's organisations.
objects.reality: Requires a product ecosystem, a developer base and decades of capital. Nobody starts here; companies arrive here.

objects.name: Global search engine at Google scale
objects.blurb: An index of the entire web plus the advertising system that funds it.
objects.reality: Search is a data and capital war. The workable entry is vertical search inside one industry.

objects.name: Global social network at Meta scale
objects.blurb: Billions of users, moderation at scale and an advertising machine.
objects.reality: Network effects protect the incumbent. A niche community is the realistic entry.

objects.name: Smartphone ecosystem at Apple scale
objects.blurb: Hardware, an operating system, an app store and a services business.
objects.reality: Requires chip design, manufacturing partners and a developer ecosystem measured in millions.

objects.name: Rocket and constellation at SpaceX scale
objects.blurb: Reusable launch, a satellite constellation and a launch site.
objects.reality: Reusability took SpaceX two decades and repeated failures. Small launch is the realistic entry.

objects.name: Automaker at Toyota scale
objects.blurb: Global factories, supplier networks, dealers and model lines.
objects.reality: Toyota-scale production is a national industrial project with decades of supplier development.

objects.name: Aircraft manufacturer at Boeing scale
objects.blurb: Certificated airframes, engine partnerships and a decades-long order book.
objects.reality: Certification alone takes years. A realistic entry is parts, interiors or drones.

objects.name: Semiconductor foundry at TSMC scale
objects.blurb: Leading-edge fabs, water and power contracts, and process know-how.
objects.reality: Each generation costs more than the last. Fabless chip design is the accessible route.

objects.name: Oil major at Exxon scale
objects.blurb: Reserves, upstream, refining, chemicals and a global trading desk.
objects.reality: Requires sovereign-scale reserves and a century of accumulated assets.

objects.name: Global bank at JPMorgan scale
objects.blurb: Balance sheet, capital ratios, regulators in every market and technology.
objects.reality: Banking licences are granted per country against capital that no individual can raise.

objects.name: Pharmaceutical major at Pfizer scale
objects.blurb: A pipeline, trials, regulatory approvals and a global sales force.
objects.reality: A single approved drug can cost a billion. A portfolio at this scale is a public company.

objects.name: Global shipping line at Maersk scale
objects.blurb: Vessels, container fleets, terminals and route networks.
objects.reality: Asset heavy and cyclical. A niche trade lane is the realistic entry.

objects.name: Global cloud provider at AWS scale
objects.blurb: Data centres in dozens of regions with custom hardware and networking.
objects.reality: Built on a decade of capital spending and an existing enterprise customer base.

objects.name: National electricity grid
objects.blurb: Transmission lines, substations, control rooms and regulators.
objects.reality: Owned or regulated by governments; a private developer can only build one project on the edge.

objects.name: National health system
objects.blurb: Hospitals, clinics, staff and funding across a whole country.
objects.reality: A state function. Private operators sell services into it, not replace it.

objects.name: National university system
objects.blurb: Campuses, faculties, research funding and accreditation across a country.
objects.reality: Requires endowment, land and accreditation built over generations.

objects.name: New planned city
objects.blurb: Land, roads, water, power, housing and decades of construction.
objects.reality: Only governments and sovereign funds attempt this; the record of private attempts is poor.

objects.name: Metro rail system
objects.blurb: Tunnels, stations, rolling stock and a public procurement process.
objects.reality: A public procurement, not a startup. Suppliers to the project are the investable layer.

objects.name: International airport
objects.blurb: Runways, terminals, navigation systems and airline agreements.
objects.reality: Land, noise studies and airline commitments make this a government project.

objects.name: Container port
objects.blurb: Berths, cranes, dredging and rail connections.
objects.reality: Granted by a port authority on waterfront that is almost never privately available.

objects.name: National defense contractor at Lockheed scale
objects.blurb: Classified programmes, cleared staff and multi-decade government contracts.
objects.reality: Entry is as a supplier or a services subcontractor, not as a prime.

objects.name: Global telecom carrier at national scale
objects.blurb: Spectrum, towers, fibre and a national regulatory licence.
objects.reality: Spectrum auctions and national licences are awarded through public processes.
